messages:
tara: Quick convo — we need to settle on an internal API pattern for edge proxying. REST gateway vs gRPC passthrough? pros/cons for client gen, telemetry, and quota enforcement.

mike: Short take: gRPC everywhere wins for perf and bidi streaming, but we pay in client support for browsers and some mobile.

nisha: Agreed on perf. Also gRPC makes per-request tracing simpler (context propagation). But we still need human-friendly JSON for debugging and curl.

ben: What about a hybrid: proto-first services + grpc-gateway to expose JSON endpoints at the edge? keeps internal topo gRPC, external is REST.

alexa: That's the grpc-gateway approach — solid. But it means double-surface testing and more CI. Also generated JSON->proto mapping can be leaky for some edge cases (maps, oneofs).

sam: From infra side: Envoy supports both. We could do an L7 gateway that translates REST->gRPC for internal services + direct gRPC passthrough for trusted callers. Routing policy based on client TLS or header.

tara: Important: quotas & rate limits. Do we enforce at edge or service? If at edge, need to map incoming REST routes to proto methods for per-route quotas.

mike: Enforcing at edge is nice for cost controls — drops traffic before it hits GPU. But that requires consistent canonical routing metadata in the gateway.

nisha: Also we want token-level cost telemetry: tokens per request, model version, model fallback. Gateway needs to enrich spans with model metadata.

ben: For rollout UX: prefer canary by header + transparent fallback. If gateway can rewrite to an older proto/service on failures, that smooths rollouts.

alexa: Danger: dual-surface increases chance of compatibility drift between proto and JSON surfaces. Need auto-generated tests that do golden roundtrips.

sam: On client gen: proto-first gives us stable typed SDKs for backend services. For web/mobile SDKs, we can publish a thin JS/TS wrapper around the REST surface. Keeps ergonomics for frontend teams.

tara: What about streaming? Some of the inference codepaths benefit from server-streaming or bidi. grpc-web has limitations — we'd need streaming fallback (chunked HTTP+ SSE) for browsers.

mike: Right — streaming is a main reason to keep native gRPC internal. Expose chunked JSON streams for browsers. That means our SDKs will need to handle both.

nisha: Observability: prefer structured spans emitted from service with method proto names. Edge should attach client id, quota bucket, and routing decision. Then Console can show per-route/policy cost.

ben: Implementation complexity estimate: grpc-first + gateway + SDK wrappers ~4-6 wks core + CI/tests + docs. If we go REST-first and translate to proto inside services, we lose typed contracts upstream.

alexa: Also consider liveness and graceful degradation. If gateway translation fails, have a config flag to passthrough to a REST compatibility shim or return 503 with a clear error code for clients to fallback gracefully.

sam: Security: mutual TLS for internal gRPC calls is straightforward. For external REST, rely on token auth + WAF. Gateway should inject identity into gRPC metadata for downstream authz checks.

tara: Can we standardize an edge->service metadata header set? e.g., x-rw-client-id, x-rw-route, x-rw-quota-bucket, x-rw-model? make docs and linters enforce it.

mike: Yes. And add a proto option like (redwood.route_info) = "route/name" so codegen picks it up. Then gateway can read it from compiled descriptors.

nisha: For rollout UI: Console should let product teams declare canary criteria tied to observability signals (latency, error-rate, model-quality delta). Gateway toggles route mapping accordingly.

ben: To reduce double-surface drift, CI should run an integration test that 1) calls JSON endpoint, 2) converts payload to proto via generated code, 3) hits gRPC service, 4) compares responses. Fail on semantically different outputs.

alexa: Agree. We should also add a small fuzz like invalid enum strings to catch mapping issues.

sam: Ops note: Envoy rate limit filter can enforce quotas per client id, but we need stable mapping. If we use proto option + descriptor registry, we can centralize mapping in the control plane.

tara: Any blockers for proto-first + grpc-gateway? I want a thumbs up or list of showstoppers.

mike: thumbs up from infra for performance. Major risk is client work for browsers and legacy mobile.

nisha: thumbs up from ML infra, but we need the telemetry hooks documented and a proto option for model metadata.

ben: I'm +1 provided we add the CI golden-roundtrip check and SDK wrappers for frontend.

alexa: +1 with caveat: schedule time for JSON->proto edge cases and add a lint rule to flag problematic proto features (maps in top-level JSON, complicated oneofs).

ci-bot: Deploy check: proto-lint failed on api/serving/v1/inference.proto: avoid top-level map fields. See CI output: https://ci.redwood.example/2468/logs

tara: Perfect — that CI failure surfaced the exact incompatibility we were worried about. I'll draft the proto options and an RFC for the mapping + gating CI tests.

mike: Cool. I'll open a work item for gateway descriptor registry + Envoy config template.

tara: Thanks all. We'll converge on proto-first + grpc-gateway, gateway-enforced quotas, and CI golden-roundtrip tests. Follow-ups: RFC, proto option PR, and SDK wrappers for JS. :thumbsup:
